free_tier.stated: The maximum file size you can upload is 256 GB or 12 hours, whichever is less.
free_tier.notes: Headline offer; binding constraint specified in limits.

per_object_cap.stated: 256 GB or 12 hours per upload, whichever is less
per_object_cap.notes: The maximum file size you can upload is 256 GB or 12 hours, whichever is less.

retention.stated: You understand and agree, however, that YouTube may retain, but not display, distribute, or perform, server copies of your videos that have been removed or deleted.
retention.notes: You understand and agree, however, that YouTube may retain, but not display, distribute, or perform, server copies of your videos that have been removed or deleted.

egress.terms: Free and unmetered. Playback and yt-dlp retrieval are served from Google's CDN at no cost; there is no egress meter on the account.

tooling: yt-dlp (youtube extractor, verified present in `yt-dlp --list-extractors`; 1752 extractors total). Binary-in-video: freddiev4/yts3 (FFV1/DCT + fountain codes, 2 stars, pushed 2026-02), KKarmugil/Infinite_Storage_Glitch (188 stars, Python ISG port), karaketir16/file2video (70 stars).
chaining: Unlimited files per channel x unlimited free Google accounts. Each upload is independently 256 GB-capped, so capacity = N accounts x M videos x 256 GB. Upload throughput, not quota, is the binding constraint.
limits_note: A daily upload-count cap exists but Google does not publish the number; its own tier page only distinguishes 'limited daily limit' (unverified) from 'higher daily limit' (phone-verified). The Data API v3 path is capped near 6 uploads/day (~1600 quota units each against a 10,000/day budget). 12-hour duration ceiling means a 256 GB file must average 47 Mbps to be reachable.

identity_cost.detail: a verified account: a verification code arrives by text message on a mobile device or by an automated voice call

reliability_note: From a datacenter IP, yt-dlp hit `Sign in to confirm you're not a bot` on 2 of 3 probe videos and HTTP 429 on the watch page. Retrieval reliably needs cookies or a residential egress. Data does not vanish, but the account can be terminated and the whole channel with it.
confidence_note: the per-upload ceiling is quoted from the first-party support page
